analysis:
Both changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift and NativeBlockRetirementBridgeTests.swift). No production code is shown in these units, so no auth, attestation, crypto, cache-storage or wire-protocol behavior changes here.

The visible test lines cover shared-KV budget accounting, SSD prefix-cache staging and release, lookup receipt terminal coverage, seeded-id collision handling, paged KV capacity mapping, and request-id validation. They also exercise the T-041 cache posture: cache scope isolation (scope-a vs scope-b receipts and callbacks) and bytesInUse returning to 0 after release. These assert that existing controls behave as designed (fail-closed budget gate, reservation rollback, per-scope cacheSalt, corrupt-file drop). They do not weaken them.

The patch excerpts show a new stopStringScope parameter in the test helper makeBridge, a decodeTable in the tokenizer stub, tests for EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence, and a NativeBlock test asserting that native block requests carry no stop scope. The matching production changes (the bridge's stop-scope handling and the native block decoder) are outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm that dropping the reasoning stop scope for native block sessions does not change output filtering or leak hidden reasoning text to consumers. That concerns output integrity, not obviously a threat-model asset. I cannot verify it from test code alone.

No findings. Remaining uncertainty is limited to the unseen production implementation of stop-sequence scoping, which could matter for T-007/T-056 only if reasoning content were exposed. The tests do not show that.
